nodes.title: AI Prompt Pixaroma (2. writes the full prompt)

aiPromptState.formula:
You write prompts for the Flux 2 Klein image model. Turn the short idea below into one image prompt of 50 to 80 words in plain English.

Start with the main subject and what it is doing, then the place, the light, the colors and the style: a photo, a 3D render, a painting or an illustration. Keep every detail of the idea and invent nothing that changes it. Do not put any words or letters in the picture unless the idea asks for them.

Answer with the prompt only, as one paragraph, with no title, no quotes and no notes.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Type a list of SHORT ideas, like a lighthouse in a storm, and press Run once: for every idea a local AI writes a full, detailed prompt and Klein makes the picture. Every prompt it wrote is kept in a text file.

 Steps

  1. Write one short idea per line in Prompt Pack Pixaroma.
  2. Press Run once. It queues one Run per idea.
  3. Watch the prompts appear in Save Text Pixaroma, and the pictures in the Preview.

 Change what the AI writes

  • The instruction it follows is the formula, in the gear of AI Prompt Pixaroma. Edit it to ask for another style, shorter prompts, always a photo, and so on.
  • Its seed is Fixed, so the same idea gives the same prompt. Set it to R for a new prompt each time.

 Why a queue here: Prompt Pack gives every idea its own Run, so each picture shows up as soon as it is ready and you can stop the queue at any idea. A list works too: with the latest Pixaroma nodes, AI Prompt can be fed from Prompt Each or a whole folder in ONE Run (the workflows in folder 7 do that with pictures).

 Update the Pixaroma nodes before feeding AI Prompt from a list. In ComfyUI 0.37 and newer, a language model that writes twice inside one Run crashed ComfyUI (ComfyUI issue 16441); the latest AI Prompt Pixaroma resets ComfyUI's memory between the items itself.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

What AI Prompt needs Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs. It is a fast 4-step model that can make a picture from words AND change a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3.5 4B, writes the prompts) - The language model that WRITES the prompts, Qwen3.5 4B. Klein's own text encoder can only read, it cannot write, so the writer is a separate, small model.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Prompt Pack Pixaroma (1. one short idea per line, one Run each) - One short idea per line (the New line button). Press Run once and it queues one Run per idea.
  • AI Prompt Pixaroma (2. writes the full prompt) - Runs the small Qwen3.5 4B language model on your own PC. Its formula (in the gear) tells it to turn the short idea into a full Klein prompt of 50 to 80 words. The idea comes in on the text wire, the model on the clip wire.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (3. picture size) - The picture size. Click a size; the Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma (each picture, saved) - Shows the picture of each Run and saves it into ComfyUI/output/Ideas.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Save Text Pixaroma (keeps every prompt it wrote) - Keeps every prompt the AI wrote in a list on the node and in a .txt file in ComfyUI/output/Written Prompts, and passes the prompt on to Klein.
  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

WhatTime
Writing one prompt (Qwen3.5 4B)about 2 to 3 s
The picture (1024 x 1024)about 1.7 s
One idea, start to endabout 5 s
4 ideas (the demo)about 21 s

The writer and Klein both stay loaded between Runs: together about 24 GB of models. A smaller card still works, ComfyUI moves the parts it needs, but it is slower.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (about 18 GB for Klein and its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Timed on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 32 GB of RAM:

  • Klein took about 3 to 6 times as long, about 10 s even for one picture: Klein and its text encoder (17 GB together) do not fit in 16 GB, so parts of them load again on every Run, and a second Run is no faster.
  • The AI text step took about 2 times as long.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
